record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: Are the large charged-current quasielastic-like cross sections reported by MiniBooNE compatible with the lower axial-mass result reported by NOMAD once multinucleon mechanisms, event-selection differences, and nuclear-model effects are treated consistently, or do the two experiments imply a genuine inconsistency?

evidence.quote: This brings us to a question that remains open: the compatibility of MiniBooNE results with the NOMAD one of MA = 1.05 ± 0.02(stat) ± 0.06(syst) GeV [35].
The answer is not obvious and requires further investigations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasielastic-like (CCQE-like) neutrino–nucleus scattering at intermediate energies (≈0.1–10 GeV). Two experiments report apparently discordant results when their data are interpreted within the relativistic Fermi gas model with a single effective axial mass M_A in the nucleon axial form factor F_A(Q²) = g_A / (1 + Q²/M_A²)²:

(i) A flux-averaged measurement on a CH₂ target (mean neutrino energy ≈ 800 MeV) yields a CCQE-like cross section on carbon that, when fitted with the relativistic Fermi gas model, requires an effective axial mass M_A^{eff} ≈ 1.35 GeV.

(ii) A measurement on a heavier nuclear target at higher mean neutrino energies (≈ 3–100 GeV), using a different event selection that requires an identified outgoing proton track, yields M_A = 1.05 ± 0.02(stat) ± 0.06(syst) GeV, consistent with the world average from deuterium data.

Multinucleon (2p2h / meson-exchange-current) interaction channels, in which the neutrino interacts with a correlated pair of nucleons and ejects two nucleons, are not included in the relativistic Fermi gas baseline but contribute to the CCQE-like sample of (i) while being largely rejected by the proton-track selection of (ii). In addition, the two analyses use different nuclear targets and different procedures for reconstructing neutrino energy and selecting events.

Question: Within a unified theoretical framework that incorporates (a) a consistent treatment of nuclear effects (Fermi motion, Pauli blocking, RPA correlations, realistic spectral functions), (b) the multinucleon (2p2h) contributions, and (c) the experiment-specific event-selection criteria and energy-reconstruction procedures, can both measurements be simultaneously described with a single value of the nucleon axial mass M_A consistent with the deuterium world average (≈ 1.0 GeV), or do the two datasets imply a genuine, model-independent inconsistency?
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple analyses (Nieves et al., spectral-function approaches, SuperScaling models, and generator-level studies in NEUT/GENIE) report that once 2p2h/meson-exchange-current contributions and improved nuclear models (RPA, spectral functions) are included with experiment-specific selections, the two measurements can be reconciled with an axial mass close to the deuterium world average (~1.0 GeV). However, residual tensions persist across generators and with additional datasets (MINERvA, T2K), so no single fully consistent description is universally accepted; the issue is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The nucleon axial mass and the MiniBooNE CCQE neutrino-nucleus data
status_evidence.snippet: MiniBooNE measurements are fully compatible with former determinations of nucleon axial mass... M_A = 1.08 ± 0.03 GeV when RPA and multinucleon knockout are included.
status_evidence.claim: Including 2p2h and RPA reconciles MiniBooNE with the world-average axial mass.

status_evidence.title: Neutrino and antineutrino CCQE scattering in the SuperScaling Approximation from MiniBooNE to NOMAD energies
status_evidence.snippet: Within the SuperScaling Approximation, both MiniBooNE and NOMAD data can be described consistently when 2p2h MEC contributions are included.
status_evidence.claim: Independent framework also reconciles the two datasets.

status_evidence.title: Testing CCQE and 2p2h models in the NEUT neutrino interaction generator
status_evidence.snippet: Comparison of CCQE+2p2h models against MiniBooNE and MINERvA shows residual model dependence; no single model describes all datasets perfectly.
status_evidence.claim: Tensions remain across datasets, indicating only partial resolution.
